conflicts.description: Solenoids 33-36 are wired through the Fliptronic II board's upper-flipper power/hold driver-transistor pairs, which this machine, having no physical upper flippers, uses for other devices. Pinned PinMAME's own src/wpc/core.h macros name CORE_FIRSTUFLIPSOL(33)/34 as sURFlipPow/sURFlip -- the upper-RIGHT circuit -- and 35/36 as sULFlipPow/sULFlip -- the upper-LEFT circuit. This manual's own printed Solenoid/Flasher Table (page 120, printed 3-8) pairs the addresses with the circuits the opposite way round: 'Up Lt. F. Power/Hold' (J907-2/J907-1, Q1/Q5, J902-3/J902-1) at 33/34 and 'Up Rt. F. Power/Hold' (J907-5/J907-4, Q2/Q7, J902-6/J902-4) at 35/36. Its own Fliptronic II Flipper Circuits page (page 130, printed 3-18) agrees with the table's side labels for those pins, J902-3/J902-1 driving the upper-left flipper position and J902-6/J902-4 the upper-right, but names no solenoid number. Neither the device functions (Up/Down Post Diverter, Right Gate, Castle Release Post, Left Gate Actuator) nor their public addresses are in doubt on any source: the manual's function column, PinMAME's drac.c (sTopDiverter 33, sRGate 34, sCastleRelease 35, sLGate 36) and the retained script's SolCallback(33..36) bindings agree. Only which driver pair, pin and wire underlies each address disagrees, and the board settles that: Twilight Zone's known-working script drives its upper-right flipper from public 33/34 and its manual wires that flipper on Q2/Q7 (J902-6/J902-4), and the solenoid tables of twelve other Fliptronic II and WPC-95 machines in this repository put 33/34 on J902-6/J902-4 and 35/36 on J902-3/J902-1, as PinMAME's names do, with transistors Q2/Q7 and Q1/Q5 except The Shadow's main table, which prints Q2 and Q7 beside J902-3 and J902-1 on its 35/36 rows while its own flipper rows print Q1 and Q5 for those pins. This manual's 3-8 table is the outlier. Resolution path: already settled by that cross-machine evidence; a photograph or continuity check of a production Dracula harness at J902 would confirm the pin each device's wire lands on.
conflicts.rationale: A naming and board-designator disagreement, not a conflict (runbook, What is not a conflict): PinMAME's macro names and the manual's printed table differ only on which upper-flipper side, driver transistor pair, pin and wire each address uses, while the manual's function column, PinMAME's drac.c and the retained script agree on every device and its public address, so nothing a recreation consumes is in doubt. Structured wiring follows the circuit agreeing independent sources give each address, with this machine's own pin and wire colour for that circuit; the excerpt keeps the printed rows literally and each device note states both readings.

conflicts.description: How many playfield bulbs solenoid 19 (3-Bank / House flasher) drives. The 3-8 Solenoid/Flasher Table prints '(1) #89' for the playfield function and '(1) #906' for the backbox one, and the Williams tech chart prints the same row ('19 3-BANK / HOUSE FLASHER ... #89(1) #906(1)'); the two may share ancestry. The 2-45 Solenoid/Flasher Location drawing prints two callouts 19 on the playfield, one beside the middle 3-bank below jet bumper 13 and one at the playfield's left edge behind the left 3-bank, both legible, and the retained known-working script drives a light at each (Flasher19 sets F19 and F19a). Every other flasher's playfield count on the 3-8 table matches its callouts on the drawing. The 3-9 Flashlamp Wiring page names the playfield function '3-Bank's' (J126-3) and the backbox one 'House' (J125-3) without a count, and the production-machine photographs examined while curating (IPDB and Pinside galleries) cannot tell a flasher socket behind either bank from a lamp socket or show what drives it. The record keeps both drawn sockets, each validated against its callout, and counts three bulbs (two playfield, one backbox); if the tables are right the quantity is two and one of the two playfield placements is not fitted. Resolution path: run the flasher test (T.5) on a production machine and observe whether the bulb behind the left 3-bank fires together with the one at the middle 3-bank when solenoid 19 is selected, or photograph the wiring from J126-3 on an unrestored machine; any Dracula owner can obtain either.

mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest on trough switches 41-44 (Trough 1-4 Ball), Trough 1 (41) nearest the eject end. Solenoid 16 (Trough) ejects the ball resting on 41 to the shooter lane; the outhole (switch 48) feeds drained balls into the trough via solenoid 15 (Outhole). The retained script's SolRelease callback drives this directly; none of these five switches is a printed opto (column 4's inverted-switch mask row is 0x00).
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: A three-position lock lane behind the Left Ramp diverter queues balls on opto switches 57 (Castle Lock 3, entry), 54 (Castle Lock 2), and 53 (Castle Lock 1, exit, nearest the release post). Solenoid 35 (Castle Release Post, printed 'Dis. Castle Release Pst', driven through the Fliptronic II board's upper-left flipper power circuit, which this machine uses for it) retracts the post (clpost.isdropped=0) to release the queued ball at position 53 toward the shooter lane; the retained script's clpost_Timer sub restores the post 280 ms later. All three lock switches are genuine opto interrupters (A-14315/A-14316) that pinned PinMAME's inverted-switch mask normalizes (column 5 = 0x7f, rows 3/4/7).
mechanisms.label: Castle Lock lane and release post

mechanisms.behavior: A single magnet is mounted on a motor-driven carriage (solenoid 28, 'Magnet's Motor') that travels diagonally beneath the playfield between a right-side entry near the Right Gate and a left-side exit near the Left Gate. The retained script tracks the carriage's position purely in software as a 0-500 counter (MagnetPos), incremented or decremented while solenoid 28 is energized and reversing direction at each endpoint; it has no single resting coordinate. Two plain leaf limit switches confirm the carriage has reached an end of travel: switch 81 (Magnet Left, part 5647-12693-14) asserts near MagnetPos=500 (the left/exit end, feeding the Left Gate) and switch 83 (Magnet Right, same part) asserts near MagnetPos=0 (the right/entry end, feeding the Right Gate) -- neither is a printed opto. Switch 82 (Ball On Magnet) is the only genuine opto of the three (A-14315/A-14316): the retained script's MistTimer_Timer tests every ball's position against a fixed diagonal line equation representing the physical beam, independent of carriage position, and PinMAME's inverted-switch mask normalizes only this one address in column 8 (0x02). Solenoid 27 (Magnet) is the electromagnet coil itself, energized by SolMistMagnet to hold a captive ball on the carriage while it travels; the driver's own stMagnet ball-state case requires the magnet to be both energized and at the correct switch/position combination before releasing the ball toward the matching gate. The carriage rides a reversing screw below the playfield and carries, beside the coil, a light socket and bulb on a coiled cable (A-16266 Coil Magnet & Screw Assembly, printed 2-27): lamp 53 (Magnet), which lights the row of thirteen small round inserts in the playfield's mist art from below as it travels, so the light moves with the captive ball. In the retained script the carriage runs from raw (850, 864) at MagnetPos 0 to (111, 1189.16) at 500 (SetMagnetPosition), and the beam line switch 82 tests runs from (126, 1220) to (870, 885); the 2-46 switch drawing puts 83 at the right end of the path, 81 beside its left end, and ends 82's leader at the beam's left end.
mechanisms.label: Mist Magnet ball-levitation carriage

mechanisms.behavior: One-way gates admit a ball onto the Mist Magnet carriage from either side. Solenoid 34 (Right Gate, printed 'Right Gate', driven through the Fliptronic II board's upper-right flipper hold circuit) opens a gate near the top-right loop (RGate.open, plus dropping RGateWall) so a ball can fall onto the carriage from the right; solenoid 36 (Left Gate Actuator, printed 'Left Ball Gate Actuator') opens a gate near the Magnet Left Pocket opto (switch 52, LGate.open, plus dropping Wall_LO) admitting a ball from the left. The driver's own ball-state chain confirms both paths lead to stMagnet.
mechanisms.label: Left and Right Mist Magnet entry gates

mechanisms.behavior: A section of the Right Ramp raises and lowers to route the ball either up the ramp or over a hump toward the Coffin Popper. Solenoid 14 (Right Ramp Up) raises it and sets the retained script's Controller.Switch(77) True; solenoid 4 (Right Ramp Down) lowers it and clears the same public switch. The Switch Locations parts list prints a real part number for switch 77 (5647-12693-36), but the retained script sets its public state directly from the solenoid commands rather than reading a discrete sensor -- an implementation simplification, not a source disagreement.
mechanisms.label: Moving Right Ramp / Coffin Ramp section

mechanisms.behavior: A small flap near the auto-plunger lane diverts the auto-launched ball either up a habitrail loop (solenoid 8 energized) or lets it fall through toward the Left Loop (solenoid 8 off), per the driver's stBallLane ball-state case. No discrete switch reports this flap's position.
mechanisms.label: Shooter Ramp entry diverter

mechanisms.behavior: A spring-loaded post near the top of the playfield (printed 'Up/Dn Post Diverter', solenoid 33, driven through the Fliptronic II board's upper-right flipper power circuit) toggles the ball between two orbit/ramp paths. Left Ramp Entry (opto switch 73) senses a ball entering the diverted path.
mechanisms.label: Up/Down Post Diverter

mechanisms.behavior: A single drop target (not a bank) near the top-left lanes. Hitting it drops the target (switch 15, L. Drop Target) and reveals a rollover behind it (switch 16, L. Drop Score) that scores the ball's passage. Solenoid 25 (L. Drop Target Reset) raises it again after a delay via the retained script's SolDTUp callback. This corrects an earlier candidate note that described a '3-bank drop target' at this address; the retained script instantiates exactly one DropTarget object (`DT15`) for switch 15, and the genuine 3-bank standup-target arrays are the unrelated Left 3-bank (66/67/68) and Middle 3-bank (86/87/88) banks.
mechanisms.label: Single Left Drop Target

The function column, PinMAME's drac.c and the retained script agree on this device and its public address, so the printed pairing is a wiring detail, not a conflict (conflict.upper-flipper-circuit-side-naming is ignored).

The bulb rides on the Mist Magnet carrier: the A-16266 Coil Magnet & Screw Assembly page (printed 2-27) fits item 7, an A-16205 Light Socket & Bulb Assembly, on the carrier's bracket beside the 20-9831 coil magnet (solenoid 27), and the manual's game story says a light moves in unison with the magnet under the playfield's mist art. The Lamp Locations parts list prints lamp assembly A-11905 for this lamp, the assembly page A-16205 for the socket; both are socket-and-bulb assemblies for the one bulb. The Lamp Locations drawing (printed 2-44) prints balloon 53 with no leader at the left end of the row of thirteen small round inserts the carrier runs under, beside a free-standing arrow pointing along the row. The bulb lights those inserts from below as the carrier moves, so it travels under the row, beside the coil. The retained table has no Light for this lamp and script.vbs never reads it; instead MotorTimer_Timer steps thirteen fixed lights ml1-ml13, one under each insert, from the carriage position whenever solenoid 28 runs, a simplification of that table that ignores this lamp's state. With no fixed position, the lamp is projected onto ml7, the middle of those thirteen, at the midpoint of its travel; solenoids 27 and 28 take the carriage track itself, the ball's line, which runs about 0.04 normalized above the row.
